facts.text: Hunza is a 100 km drive from Gilgit, and the drive takes almost 2-3 hours.
facts.quote: Hunza is a 100 km drive from Gilgit

facts.text: The journey from Islamabad can take as long as 24 hours.
facts.quote: The journey from Islamabad can take as long as 24 hours

facts.text: From Kashgar there is a regular international bus service to Hunza via Sost, crossing the Khunjerab Pass.
facts.quote: regular international bus service to Hunza via Sost

facts.text: Private vehicles are normally used as local transport.
facts.quote: Private vehicles are normally used as local transport

facts.text: Renting jeeps is also a common way of moving around.
facts.quote: Renting jeeps is also a common way of moving around

facts.text: The main bus stand is on the KKH Aliabad, with booking agents in town for long-distance buses and jeeps along the KKH.
facts.quote: The main bus stand is on the KKH Aliabad

facts.text: The Khunjerab Pass is open from May 1st to Dec 30th, but closed in winter.
Rakaposhi's climate is generally favorable, with long periods of exceptional weather not uncommon throughout the summer.
facts.quote: long periods of exceptional weather are not uncommon throughout the summer

facts.text: Flights to Gilgit are subject to weather clearance, and in winters flights are often delayed by several days.
facts.quote: in winters, flights are often delayed by several days

facts.text: From Tashkurgan, you can go to immigration to get a departure approval before continuing toward Sost.
The Khunjerab Pass is about 5000 m high.
Most of the people of Hunza are Islmaili Muslims, followers of the Aga Khan.
facts.quote: Most of the people of Hunza are Islmaili Muslims
